clue.text: Puccini's fat and cunning Madame

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: A spiteful description of a stout, scheming leading lady in an Italian opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue read around the wordplay: Puccini's Madame is the heroine of his opera Madama Butterfly, with fat and cunning embedded inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cio-Cio-San, the title character of Puccini's opera, is known by her nickname Butterfly.

clue.text: Beautiful girl, one demanding a ring

parts.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them, so a bell is a demand for a ring

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman who insists on an engagement ring before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a telephone call, not jewellery: a bell is British slang for a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella is Italian for beautiful and is used in English for a pretty girl or woman.

clue.text: Immaculate type of shirt is not roughly shorter

indicators.note: roughly marks a colloquial, rough-spoken version of the phrase that follows it

explanation.surface: A spotless shirt of some style looks a little on the short side.
explanation.walkthrough: Ain't is the rough, nonstandard form of is not, which is what roughly signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaculate is without stain or blemish, which is exactly what taintless means.

clue.text: Fight for a job

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a battle or clash between forces
second meaning: a booking for a performer or employment

explanation.surface: Someone battling to land a position.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is both a military encounter and a hired spell of work such as a singer's booking.

clue.text: Healthier when swallowing river waste?

indicators.note: something swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Wondering whether drinking river water is a wasteful health fad.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money or time is to squander it bit by bit, a synonym of waste as a verb.

clue.text: Important to the taxman, eg 2006 complete

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the year-end is the date the taxman cares about

parts.note: 2006 is an example of a year

explanation.surface: The close of the 2006 tax year, a key date for the revenue man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than equals the answer: the year-end is when accounts are closed and tax is reckoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The year-end is the closing date of a financial year, crucial for tax returns and assessments.

clue.text: Brother needs help in making scrambled egg

parts.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A sibling wants a hand cooking breakfast eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrambled egg is military slang for the gold braid on a senior officer's cap peak, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled egg is the jocular name for the gold braid decorating senior officers' caps.

clue.text: Yob holds Deborah's head upside down in trunk

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upside down reads the letters from bottom to top
to hold something is to have it inside you
the head of a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A thug grabs Deborah and hangs her head-first in the boot of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The D goes in after the first letter of yob, and the whole lot is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the torso, the main part of the human body apart from head and limbs.

clue.text: Having suffered, he'd better support the account

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a/c is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A man in pain must still underwrite the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the second piece supports the first by lying under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ached is the past tense of ache, meaning having felt pain or suffered.

clue.text: Lad with Chanel applied freely where boys meet girls

indicators.note: applied freely suggests something splashed on without order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man doused in perfume heads out to pick up girls.
explanation.definitionFit: A public venue for dancing was the traditional place for young men and women to meet and court.

clue.text: Stretching out and stretching the truth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reclining at full length

explanation.surface: Someone lounging about while exaggerating their story.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying is the present participle both of lie, recline, and of lie, tell untruths.

clue.text: At a future time, should it arise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at some later point
second meaning: on condition that something happens

explanation.surface: A vague promise about acting later, conditional on circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both at whatever later moment and provided the occasion actually occurs.

clue.text: A lieutenant goes to the ball to win her completely

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
a ball is round, like the letter O
to win someone is to get them

explanation.surface: An officer attends a dance hoping to woo a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball is a round shape giving the letter O, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning totally or entirely, the same as completely.

clue.text: Red general shows superiority

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display within the words themselves

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A communist commander proves himself the better man.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over someone means having an advantage or superiority.

clue.text: Unblemished record rarely found in a dosshouse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spotless history, or a match without conceding a goal
second meaning, taken literally: freshly laundered bedding

explanation.walkthrough: A dosshouse is a very cheap lodging house for homeless people, where fresh bedding is unlikely; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a record free of offences, and literally describes laundered bed linen.

clue.text: Idealist doctor accepts me having cut ear

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: to cut into something is to get inside it

explanation.surface: A visionary physician agrees to operate on someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Me cuts into ear between its second and third letters, and the doctor stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone with unrealistic hopes, a synonym of idealist.

clue.text: Blair has a den that's wrecked, but can be made dry

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken apart and can be put back in another order

explanation.surface: The former prime minister's flooded study could still be dried out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was British prime minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainable describes something whose water can be emptied away, leaving it dry.

clue.text: Spot Emma with hat on back to front

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another sits ahead of it
back to front means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Seeing Emma wearing her hat the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a spot means being in a tricky predicament, the same as a dilemma.

clue.text: Scotsman about to get hooked on having potatoes outside

indicators.note: having something round you means wrapping it, so the rest goes within
outside says which piece is the wrapper around the others

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A Highlander becomes addicted to a dish wrapped in potato.
explanation.walkthrough: Mash is British slang for mashed potatoes. Macintosh is a Scottish surname; Charles Macintosh was the Scot who gave his name to the raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Macintosh is a Scottish clan surname, so a man called Macintosh is an example of a Scotsman.

clue.text: Racine's reformed killer

indicators.note: reformed means given a new form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: The French dramatist Racine has turned over a new leaf as a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notorious poison, a substance that kills.

clue.text: Chef that is, say, beginning to make biscuits

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chef starts to bake some biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage cookies are what the British call biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookies are small sweet baked treats, the American word for biscuits.

clue.text: Fortune left in this part of church

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Money abandoned in a part of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Meet NCO, even if drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Telling a sergeant to show up even if he is tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: An NCO is a non-commissioned officer, such as a sergeant or corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to come together or assemble, a synonym of meet as a verb.

clue.text: A number half seen showing sixth sense

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: half a word keeps only one of its two halves, here the front

parts.note: the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Someone apparently psychic, half-seeing what's coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a nose for something is an idiom for an instinct or intuition, a kind of sixth sense.

clue.text: Dismisses talk of wind instrument

indicators.note: talk of means what follows is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a sax is a saxophone, a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A bandleader fires players who keep discussing the saxophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is informal for firing them from a job, so sacks matches dismisses.

clue.text: Knowledge obtained once casing is broken

indicators.note: broken things come apart and their pieces can be reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Learning something only after cracking open a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognisance is a formal word for awareness or knowledge of something.

clue.text: Don't start to beat up and knock back

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; that the result sits inside these words is no coincidence of hiding, just what dropping a letter leaves

explanation.surface: A plea not to start a fight and to refuse what's offered.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock back here means consume quickly, not reject.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back food or drink is slang for consuming it, the same as eating it up.

clue.text: Exclamation heard as I sway, losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone cries out as they stagger, feeling faint.
explanation.walkthrough: Heard as is just a link, not a homophone signal: the exclamation is heard as someone sways.
explanation.definitionFit: I say is a dated British interjection expressing surprise or seeking attention.

clue.text: Slip as a learner in reverse

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: the reverse of something is its back side

explanation.surface: A learner driver skids while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse is not a gear or a direction here but the back side of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to slip back into bad habits, a lapse or relapse.

clue.text: Swallow about half a bowl from vessel

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to swallow food is to eat

indicators.note: half a word keeps just one of its halves, here the front

parts.note: the front two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Gulping down some soup straight from the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: An E-boat was a German motor torpedo boat of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat is a small fast warship, so it is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Try one of William Hazlitt's?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a short literary prose piece

explanation.walkthrough: William Hazlitt was a famous English essayist of the early nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is both an attempt and a short prose composition, the form Hazlitt was known for.

clue.text: Make haste when absorbed in trade in unpleasant factory

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is taken inside it

parts.note: swop is a variant spelling of swap, to trade

indicators.note: to make something from materials is to form them into a new shape

explanation.surface: Workers rushing while busy at their jobs in a grim workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Make haste reads as hurry, but make is the anagram signal. Swop is a less common spelling of swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a factory where employees work long hours for low pay in poor conditions.
